Barone recommends foods like bananas, melons and avocados, noting that consumers should still wash them before cutting into them and peeling them. She also recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. headline: Community gathers to honor 9-year-old boy killed in dirt bike crash with FedEx truck in St. Lucie County
teaser: Family members, friends and neighbors gathered Tuesday evening to honor the life of a 9-year-old boy killed in a crash involving a dirt bike and a FedEx box tru.
body:
A 12-year-old boy injured in a dirt bike crash that killed his 9-year-old friend in St. Lucie County has been released from the hospital, according to his family's attorney.

The crash happened around 3:07 p.m. Monday in the 600 block of East Midway Road near Fort Pierce when the two boys, riding together on a dirt bike, collided with a FedEx box truck, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The 9-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene. The 12-year-old was taken to a local hospital in stable condition.

Steven Baker, the attorney representing the 12-year-old's family, returned to the scene Tuesday where markings still lined the sidewalk. He said the child has a few broken bones and a fractured tooth. The boy is progressing physically but is also recovering mentally from the trauma of the crash, Baker said, adding that the child needs time with his parents and will never be able to forget the incident.

Family members, friends and neighbors gathered Tuesday evening in St. Lucie County to honor the life of the 9-year-old boy. The vigil was held less than 24 hours after the crash on East Midway Road. Although the Florida Highway Patrol has not publicly released the victim's identity, loved ones came together to remember the young boy with candles, balloons and prayers.

Neighbors said the area is a common place for children and others to ride bicycles and dirt bikes.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said that since 2020, there have been 110 bike crashes in St. Lucie County, 15 of them involving children. On Midway Road specifically, there have been six reported crashes, two of which have involved children. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro called the crash a stark reminder.

The Florida Highway Patrol continues to investigate what led to the collision.

headline: Zayas Homers Twice as St. Lucie Mets Cruise Past Mighty Mussels
teaser:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

body:
Julio Zayas homered twice and Trey Snyder continued his hot stretch at the plate as the St. Lucie Mets defeated the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels 8-2 Tuesday night at Clover Park.

The victory in the series opener was St. Lucie's fifth win in its last six games.

The Mets held a 1-0 lead through two innings before breaking the game open with four runs against Fort Myers starter Eric Hammond in the third.

Randy Guzman drew a bases-loaded walk to bring home the first run of the inning. Snyder followed with a two-run double before scoring on a throwing error after Antonio Jimenez singled, extending the Mets' lead to 5-0.

Jimenez added a sacrifice fly in the fifth inning to make it 6-0.

Zayas provided the rest of St. Lucie's offense with solo home runs in the sixth and eighth innings. He became the second Mets player this season to record a multi-homer game, joining Guzman.

Zayas finished 3-for-4 with his fifth and sixth home runs of the season.

Snyder also went 3-for-3 with a double, a walk, two RBIs and a run scored. He has collected seven hits over his last two games.

St. Lucie starter Conner Ware pitched three scoreless innings, allowing no runs while striking out four.

Emilio Obispo earned the win after allowing two runs on two hits over four innings. He walked three and struck out three.

Zack Mack pitched a scoreless eighth inning before Elwis Mijares worked the ninth and induced a 4-6-3 double play to end the game.

The Mets improved to 9-14 in the second half and 42-47 overall. The Mighty Mussels fell to 10-13 in the second half and 47-41 overall.

The teams will play the second game of the series Wednesday at Clover Park. The Mets will hold their annual Summer Camp Day, with first pitch scheduled for 11:10 a.m.
